WIZARD STUDY — A four-meter circular tower study, rough-cut limestone walls furred with old tapestry maps, vaulted ceiling of dark oak ribs, leaded-glass window casting violet-amber light across a partners desk buried under annotated folios. Built-in alcoves hold glowing crystals and wax-sealed scroll-cases. A low hearth crackles behind a wingback chair, its armrests worn smooth. Candle-stubs crowd every horizontal surface; dripped wax has calcified into small white stalactites along the shelf edges.

HEDGEWITCH HUT — Timber-frame cottage interior, roughly five meters by four, wattle-and-daub walls hung with braided garlic, dried lavender, and bundled nightshade. Heavy thatch overhead, smoke-blackened rafters strung with herb-bundles and small carved-bone charms. A single deep-set window with thick bull's-eye panes glows green-gold from the herb garden beyond. A clay hearth dominates one wall, iron pot hanging above embers. The plank floor is worn pale underfoot, scattered with rush mats and spilled poppy seeds.

ALCHEMIST LAB — A stone-walled workshop, perhaps six meters by four, barrel-vaulted ceiling of pale limestone soot-stained above a central distillation rig of copper tubing and blown-glass alembics. Shelves of apothecary bottles line every wall, labelled in cramped alchemical script, their contents glowing faint amber, green, and cobalt. A wrought-iron forge-corner holds a small furnace and sand-bath. Stained oak workbench, brass scales mid-use, residue rings marking years of experiments into the grain of the wood.

DRAGON-LORE LIBRARY — A long scholar's reading room, stone-ribbed ceiling low enough to touch, built into the belly of an old keep. Dragon-bone shelves—pale, enormous, smoothly fitted—hold oversized folios bound in scaled leather. A juvenile skull is mounted above the fireplace, jaw propped open with an iron rod. Leaded-glass windows, narrow as arrow-slits but taller, spill cold blue light across the reading table heaped with rubbings, claw-print castings, and half-unrolled parchment maps tracing ancient migration corridors.

OBSERVATORY TOWER-TOP — The uppermost chamber of a stone spire, barely four meters across, domed ceiling of lime-plastered brick painted with a fading celestial chart, constellation lines still traced in gilt. A brass orrery the size of a cartwheel turns slowly on a central post, candlelight playing off its rings. A slit-dome oculus can be cranked open above the viewing stool. Every wall is papered to wainscot height with annotated star-charts, pinned and overlapping, edges amber with age.

FORGE-HALL READING CORNER — A stone-vaulted alcove cut into the wall of a Dwarven forge-hall, barely large enough for a high-backed settle and a low iron-banded table. Carved geometric knotwork frames the arch. The forge-heat from the main hall makes the corner perpetually warm; a small brazier of coals supplements. Shelves of hand-width cut into the stone hold ledgers, folded survey-maps, and rune-stamped ingot-books. Tallow candles in iron sconces. The floor is slate, worn to a near-mirror shine by boots across generations.

WIZARD-TOWER PRIVATE CHAMBER — A circular room high in a personal spire, five meters across, walls of coursed ashlar hung with faded star-maps and a single gilt-framed portrait of an unsmiling predecessor. Two arrow-slit windows fitted with leaded rounds admit thin red sunset light. A spiral iron stair coils up through the floor to the roof-platform above. Bookshelves fill every arc of wall, interrupted only by the hearth, above which a scrying-mirror in a tarnished silver frame leans slightly forward, always fogged.

SAGE'S VAULT — An underground sanctum cut from living rock, roughly four meters square, ceiling low and barrel-arched with runes carved into every keystone and glowing with a cold blue-white inner light. Access is via a single iron-bound door whose lintel bears a warding inscription. Shelves of black ironwood hold clay-sealed scroll-jars. A central reading plinth of pale stone holds an open codex under a preservation-glass dome. Two bronze cressets burn without apparent fuel. The air smells of mineral dust and old vellum.

ALCHEMIST APOTHECARY — A ground-floor apothecary workroom, stone-flagged floor, plaster walls entirely obscured by floor-to-ceiling shelving of dark walnut packed with ranked apothecary jars—blown glass, earthenware, stopped with cork and wax, each labelled in three ink-colours. A low counter bisects the room, its surface a scarred record of years of cutting, grinding, and spillage. Copper mortars of every size stand in descending order. A small leaded casement window above the counter lets in afternoon light; a tallow lamp supplements at the counter's near end where a cauldron simmers on its trivet.
